rules.title: Prefer direct medical providers
rules.rule_text: For provider-network research, prioritize clinics, hospitals, laboratories, diagnostic centers, and physician practices that directly perform the requested service. Avoid referral platforms, network managers, occupational-health consultancies, and other intermediary layers unless explicitly requested.

rules.title: Occu-Med is not a TPA
rules.rule_text: Do not describe Occu-Med as a third-party administrator or treat TPA/claims-administration opportunities as in scope.

rules.title: Provider documents findings; Occu-Med performs medical review
rules.rule_text: Treat the examining provider as documenting findings and requested test results. Do not represent the provider as making Occu-Med’s employment/deployment recommendation unless a program specifically requires it.

rules.title: Workers’ compensation is excluded from current Occu-Med service scope
rules.rule_text: Do not classify or pursue workers’ compensation treatment, claims management, MPN/provider-panel enrollment, utilization review, managed care, or other workers’ compensation network/claims services as Occu-Med offerings.

policies.title: Consult Occu-Med Core before acting
policies.instruction: Before answering an Occu-Med-specific question, retrieve applicable current hard rules, then current facts/relationships, then supporting source material. Higher-authority current information overrides lower-authority or historical information.

policies.title: Do not convert historical context into current service scope
policies.instruction: Historical discussion of workers’ compensation, claims, deployment incidents, or other topics does not make them current Occu-Med service offerings. Current canonical rules control scope.

policies.title: Do not store referral counts by default
policies.instruction: For Occu-Med Core ingestion, preserve exact client presence, program relationships, locations, service scope, requirements, capabilities, and contract relationships. Do not store referral counts, referral shares, or other volume metrics unless the operator explicitly asks for quantitative analytics.

policies.title: Independent medical evaluation requires employment context
policies.instruction: Treat IME / Independent Medical Evaluation as in scope only when the opportunity is for employment-related fitness-for-duty, return-to-work, medical qualification, or similar employee evaluation. Do not treat workers’ compensation claims IMEs, claims administration, or injury treatment as in scope.

policies.title: Interpret Occu-Med IME as employment fitness/return-to-work evaluation
policies.instruction: When Occu-Med uses Independent Medical Evaluation (IME), interpret it as an employment-related medical evaluation by a qualified examining clinician to determine whether an employee can safely return to work or perform job duties. Do not interpret this capability as workers’ compensation benefit eligibility, claim adjudication, impairment rating/award work, claims administration, or workers’ compensation treatment. Because external RFPs may use IME for workers’ compensation, review surrounding scope before treating IME language as in-scope.

policies.title: Treat documented service capabilities as non-exhaustive
policies.instruction: Services listed in the Occu-Med Provider Service Agreement are documented examples of services Occu-Med can contract or coordinate through its provider network. Never treat this list as exhaustive, exclusive, or as a reason to conclude that an unlisted service is unavailable. For a requested service not in the documented capability table, classify it as unknown/not-yet-documented and investigate whether Occu-Med can source or arrange it. Do not infer that Occu-Med itself directly performs the clinical service, and do not infer that every provider or location offers it.

policies.title: Preserve provenance
policies.instruction: Every imported fact, relationship, rule, government record, and knowledge chunk should retain a source reference and locator when available.

policies.title: Refresh time-sensitive official status records
policies.instruction: If an official registration, license, certification, contract status, or similar source has passed its stated expiration or validity date, do not present its prior status as current. Flag it for refresh and preserve the historical snapshot.

policies.title: Surface conflicts rather than silently merging them
policies.instruction: When sources disagree, preserve both claims, mark the conflict, and prefer the current higher-authority source for action while retaining provenance.

policies.title: Unlisted service is not excluded
policies.instruction: Absence of a service from the documented service-capability table must never be interpreted as out of scope or unavailable. Occu-Med can often arrange additional services by sourcing an appropriate provider. Treat unlisted services as needing verification/sourcing unless a separate canonical rule explicitly excludes them.

policies.title: Use public client classifications only
policies.instruction: Do not store internal client segmentation or roster labels in Occu-Med Core. For client industry or sector, use only externally recognized classifications from authoritative public sources. Prefer exact public procurement, registration, or NAICS classifications when available; otherwise leave the classification unset rather than inventing one.
